questions.q: Why does dw.DimProduct's load use LEFT JOIN against Production.ProductSubcategory and ProductCategory instead of INNER JOIN?
options: LEFT JOIN runs faster regardless of the data
Production.Product.ProductSubcategoryID is nullable for some real products, and an INNER JOIN would silently drop those products out of the warehouse entirely
INNER JOIN is not valid syntax in SQL Server
Because Production.ProductCategory has duplicate rows
questions.explain: Some real products (raw materials, components) have no subcategory at all. LEFT JOIN keeps every product, with CategoryName/SubcategoryName simply NULL where there's nothing to flatten.

questions.q: Where does dw.DimCustomer's CustomerType column come from?
options: It's copied directly from a CustomerType column in Sales.Customer
It's derived during the load with a CASE expression based on whether StoreID is populated
It's manually entered by Finance after the load
It's calculated in Power BI, not the warehouse
questions.explain: CustomerType doesn't exist anywhere in AdventureWorks2012 — it's derived once during the warehouse load from the real fact that StoreID is populated for store accounts and null for individuals.

questions.q: Why is dw.DimDate built with a recursive CTE instead of a simple SELECT against a source table?
options: Because AdventureWorks2012 has no table listing every calendar date, so the date range has to be generated
Because Sales.SalesOrderHeader.OrderDate is stored as text
Because recursive CTEs are faster than any other method for any table
Because dw.DimDate doesn't actually need every date, only order dates
questions.explain: There's no 'table of all dates' in the OLTP source, so dw.DimDate is generated directly, covering the real range of OrderDate values with a recursive CTE.

questions.q: Why does the recursive CTE building dw.DimDate need OPTION (MAXRECURSION 0)?
options: To disable logging during the insert
SQL Server defaults to a 100-row recursion limit, which a multi-year date range would hit almost immediately without it
To force the dates to be generated in descending order
It has no real effect and is just a style convention
questions.explain: MAXRECURSION 0 removes the default 100-iteration cap so the CTE can generate every date across the full multi-year range.

questions.q: Why must Sales.SalesTerritory's Group column be written as [Group] in a T-SQL query?
options: Because GROUP is a T-SQL reserved word and needs brackets to be used as a plain column name
Because Group is spelled differently in the real table
Because it's a computed column requiring special syntax
Brackets are only cosmetic and have no real effect
questions.explain: GROUP is a reserved keyword in T-SQL (used in GROUP BY), so referencing a column literally named Group requires bracketing it as [Group].
